title: Capture Cursor agent-transcript schema from a real Mac
description:
Capture and pin the agent-CLI transcript format from a real Mac: JSONL transcripts at ~/.cursor/projects/<sanitized-path>/agent-transcripts/<session-id>/<session-id>.jsonl (the project path with slashes replaced by dashes), with per-session metadata in ~/.cursor/chats/<workspace-hash>/<session-id>/store.db. The line-level schema (type, role, text, timestamp fields) is not publicly documented — pin it from real files before writing extraction. Also check whether older plain-text .txt transcripts coexist. Record findings; never commit real transcripts.

Done when: the line schema is documented from real files, synthetic fixtures encode it, and findings record the evidence.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: **Blocked from remote capture — needs Ryan's real Mac.** Cannot pin the agent-transcript line schema or check legacy .txt transcripts from this environment. Before implementing locally, capture from `~/.cursor/projects/<sanitized-path>/agent-transcripts/<session-id>/<session-id>.jsonl` and `~/.cursor/chats/<workspace-hash>/<session-id>/store.db`: (1) the exact line-level JSONL schema (type, role, text, timestamp field names and value shapes); (2) whether user lines are distinguishable from injected context at line level; (3) whether older plain-text .txt transcripts coexist in the same tree; (4) store.db table/column layout. Never commit real transcripts — encode into synthetic fixtures under tests/fixtures/sentiment/cursor/ and record findings here. Until then, the Cursor agent-transcript extractor in KDATAP-d3d98c runs against a best-documented tolerant shape (JSON object per line, role field, text/string content, epoch-ms timestamp) validated only against synthetic fixtures.
